title: A projective localization of a finite module of finite projective dimension is stably free
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $T\subset R$ a multiplicative submonoid, and $M$ a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] of projective dimension at most $n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. Let $N$ be a localization of $M$ at $T$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], with compatible $T^{-1}R$-module structure, and suppose $N$ is projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Suppose the ring and the module types lie in the same universe, as in the attached source declaration. Then $N$ is stably free: there is a finite free $T^{-1}R$-module $Q$ for which $N\oplus Q$ is free [def-weil-pbc-free-module].

proof.text: Induct on n, following the existing proved source theorem. For n=0, M is finite projective over the local ring, hence free, and its localization is free. For the successor case, take a finite free presentation F -> M, with kernel K. Noetherianity makes K finite, and dimension shifting lowers its projective-dimension bound to n. Localization preserves injectivity, surjectivity and exactness. Because N is projective, the localized sequence splits, its localized kernel is projective, and the induction hypothesis makes that kernel stably free. Adding its stabilizing finite free summand to the split sequence shows N is stably free. This is exactly the source theorem, which is already fully proved.

      HasProjectiveDimensionLE (ModuleCat.of R M) n →
